description: Our call-centre software analyses employees' voices during calls to infer whether they are stressed, angry or bored, and shows the results to their team leaders.

A city council system scores residents on their social behaviour, such as unpaid fines and complaints from neighbours, and residents with low scores get slower access to unrelated public services like housing support.
We build a face recognition database by automatically scraping facial images from social media and the open web, without targeting anyone in particular, and sell searches against it.

A mobile game for young children uses AI to detect when a child is most impulsive and then shows manipulative prompts designed to push them into in-app purchases their parents would not approve, causing financial harm.

Our police-analytics product predicts the risk that a specific person will commit a crime, based only on profiling their personality traits and characteristics, with no objective facts linked to any criminal activity.
We sell software that screens CVs and ranks job applicants so recruiters know whom to invite to interviews.
A bank uses our model to evaluate the creditworthiness of consumers and set a credit score that decides whether their loan application is approved.
Universities use our proctoring software to monitor students through their webcams during online exams and flag prohibited behaviour such as cheating.
A public authority uses our system to evaluate whether people are eligible for social welfare benefits and to decide whether to grant or reduce them.
Our workforce platform monitors warehouse workers' performance and behaviour and uses it to decide promotions and terminations.
A national migration authority uses our tool to examine visa applications and assess the reliability of the evidence the applicants provide.

Our AI software analyses MRI scans and is the diagnostic function of a medical device that must go through third-party conformity assessment by a notified body under the EU Medical Devices Regulation.

We make the AI vision module that acts as the safety component of an industrial robot, stopping the machine when a person enters its working zone. The robot is machinery that needs third-party conformity assessment.
Our AI controls the emergency braking of passenger lifts as their safety component; the lifts fall under the EU Lifts Directive and require third-party conformity assessment.
Our HR tool only books interview slots in recruiters' calendars after the recruiters have chosen whom to invite. It does not score, rank or filter anyone.
After teachers have graded and written feedback on students' final exams, our tool only corrects the spelling and grammar of the teachers' written feedback. It never changes or influences the grades.

A bank uses our tool to detect patterns in loan officers' past credit decisions and flag deviations for a human review. It does not replace or influence the officers' assessments and does not profile applicants.
A chatbot on our online shop talks directly with customers to answer questions about orders, deliveries and returns.
Our marketing tool generates realistic synthetic images and videos of people who appear to be real, for use in advertising campaigns.
Our system writes news articles about local events and publishes them on our website to inform the public, with no human editorial review.
An AI voice agent phones restaurant customers to confirm and change their table bookings, holding a natural spoken conversation with them.
An email spam filter that sorts incoming messages into the inbox or spam folder for our staff.
A model that forecasts weekly demand for products in our warehouses so we can plan stock levels.
AI that controls the behaviour of computer-controlled opponents in our single-player video game.
A tool that predicts when our office printers will need maintenance, based on their usage logs.
An AI tool our HR team uses to help with hiring.
